classification.difficultyReason: Track two transfers based on different population groups and combine the employed remainder with the newly employed group.

content.prompt: In a particular country in 2010, $15\%$ of the population is unemployed and $85\%$ is employed. In 2011, $10\%$ of the people unemployed became employed and $10\%$ of those employed became unemployed. What percentage of the population is employed now?

answer.short:
$78\%$.

Combine those who remain employed with those who move from unemployment into employment.
answer.worked:
Take the population as $100$ units. The transfers are calculated from the two original groups.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Remaining employed}&=85\times0.90\\\text{Remaining employed}&=76.5\\\text{Newly employed}&=15\times0.10\\\text{Newly employed}&=1.5\\\text{Total employed}&=76.5+1.5\\\text{Total employed}&=78\\\text{Percentage employed}&=\frac{78}{100}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage employed}&=78\%\end{align*}$$
